page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-allocated virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, running on an Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.3 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 13.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud hardware. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng registers at 1105.58, categorized as weak, while multi-core performance drops to the bottom 10% with a score of 1452.88. Memory bandwidth tests show uncached read speeds of 13.32 GB/sec and write speeds of 11.13 GB/sec. Geekbench evaluations yield a single-core score of 944.0 and a multi-core score of 1124.0, reflecting its legacy hardware profile.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-2 offers a higher memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-sensitive workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. However, its lower benchmark scores indicate a performance tradeoff compared to newer instance generations. This instance is best suited for lightweight databases, basic caching layers, or small-scale web serving applications that benefit from its 13.0 GB memory footprint but have low processing demands.
